bull_bear.body:
- Ownership of two land-anchored luxury hotel assets in the two largest Indian hospitality markets - Hotel Hyatt Regency in Mumbai (direct) and the JW Marriott at New Delhi Aerocity (through Aria Hotels)
- The Aerocity asset operates under an international luxury brand (J.W. Marriott) in a supply-constrained airport hospitality district
- Demonstrated brand strength of the Aerocity asset: JW Marriott New Delhi Aerocity won 'Best Luxury Hotel' at India's Best Awards 2025 by Travel & Leisure, its Mosaic Impact Award under the Luxury Segment from Marriott International, and its outlets (ADRIFT Kaya, Delhi Baking Company, Spa by JW) carried separate industry awards in 2025

bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Material uncertainty over the Company's ability to continue as a going concern — The auditors report that 'the Company's current liabilities exceed the current assets by Rs. 42,432.87 lakhs as at March 31, 2026' and that, in the absence of sufficient appropriate audit evidence to support the Company's ability to meet its obligations, a material uncertainty exists that may cast significant doubt on the entity's ability to continue as a going concern - and that the standalone financial statements neither use another acceptable basis of accounting nor adequately disclose the matter.
- The Company's own hotel is shut and generates no operations — The Company owns Hotel Hyatt Regency in Mumbai, which is 'in shut condition as on date'. The MD&A states 'the operations of the Company are not yet started after coming out from CIRP', and the Company employed only two people during the year (the Company Secretary and the Chief Financial Officer). Restart is contingent on completing a physical verification and evaluation of PPE before commencing operation, with no date given.
- The Saraf Group's option to acquire Hyatt Regency, Mumbai, and the unresolved classification of the funding it advanced — Novak Hotels Private Limited ('Saraf Group') advanced amounts to the Company under a framework agreement entered into between the promoters and the Saraf Group during the insolvency resolution process, and the agreement gives the Saraf Group an option to acquire Hyatt Regency, Mumbai. The Board obtained shareholder approval to create a charge/lien over the hotel to secure those amounts, and Novak's own audited accounts describe them as advances for acquiring the hotel - so the auditors are 'unable to state if the classification of amounts received is' appropriate. The Company's single owned asset is therefore encumbered and potentially subject to transfer.
- Fixed-asset records and physical verification are absent, so the existence of the property, plant and equipment cannot be confirmed — 'The Company has neither provided us with proper records showing full particulars, including quantitative details and situation of property, plant and equipment nor has provided us with the information regarding the physical verification of property, plant and equipment. Therefore, we are unable to comment on the existence of the property, plant' - the auditors' inability bears directly on the carrying value of the Company's principal asset.
- Unreconciled statutory dues and government-authority balances — 'Outstanding recoverable/payables balances with the Government Authorities are subject to reconciliation with the statutory records and consequential adjustment, if any', and in the absence of complete period details of statutory dues payable the auditors are unable to comment on the adequacy of interest expense recognised on those dues - an open, potentially growing liability of unknown size.
- Single-asset, single-segment, single-city concentration — 'During the period under review, the Company engaged in only one segment of Hotel Business'. All consolidated earnings arise from one subsidiary, Aria Hotels, which owns one hotel - the JW Marriott at New Delhi Aerocity - while the Company's own asset is one shut hotel in Mumbai. There is no diversification of property, brand, geography or format to absorb a shock at either site.
- Compliance and listing-status overhang carried over from insolvency — The Company was 'revived on 9th January, 2024 since than the Management is busy with doing pending compliances with respect of BSE and NSE Stock Exchange and other concerned Authorities.' Suspension of trading was only revoked after applications to both exchanges, and management bandwidth remains absorbed by the compliance backlog rather than by operations.
- Cost, labour and demand risks management flags for the hotel business — The MD&A's Risks and Concerns section flags a tight labour market and staff shortages that can compromise service quality, rising operational costs for food, utilities and wages that directly compress margins, competition from short-term rental models such as Airbnb that alter pricing structures, reputational exposure to negative social-media reviews, and data-privacy/cybersecurity risk from guest data. It also flags the Israel-Iran conflict feeding oil prices and inflation, to which India is 'particularly sensitive because it imports most of its crude oil', and a consequently cautious RBI on rate cuts.

outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The annual report discloses no capex or expansion project. The Company is in a post-insolvency rebuild rather than an expansion phase: it was revived on 9th January 2024, its own hotel - Hotel Hyatt Regency in Mumbai - is in shut condition as on date, and the only stated forward action on the asset base is that the Company is in the process of evaluating property, plant and equipment by physical verification, including the location of each item, before commencing operation. The Company's only other hotel asset is held indirectly: its 99.98% material subsidiary Aria Hotels and Consultancy Services Private Limited owns a 523-room 5-star deluxe hotel under the J.W. Marriott brand at New Delhi Aerocity, Hospitality District, near IGI Airport. There was no change in the authorised share capital during the year, and the Company had no associate or joint venture company during the financial year or as on 31st March 2026. Industry-level expansion commentary in the MD&A (asset-light expansion by hospitality operators, growth into Tier-II and Tier-III cities) is about the sector, not about any plan of this Company.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- India's hotel industry is projected to grow between 9% and 12% during FY2026, driven by strong occupancy levels and improved average room rates, with demand expected to remain resilient despite a high base effect
- Premium hotel occupancy is expected to remain robust in the range of 72-74%, while room tariffs are anticipated to witness steady growth owing to demand outpacing new supply additions in major cities
- Demand growth continued to outpace room supply in several key markets, leading to improved pricing power for hotel operators; premium room inventory growth may continue to lag demand growth over the next few years, supporting occupancy and pricing
- Demand base is domestic leisure tourism, destination weddings, religious tourism, concerts, sporting events, corporate travel and MICE; India's hospitality sector is becoming increasingly domestic-demand driven
- Sector tailwinds from increasing air connectivity, infrastructure development, digital travel platforms and rising consumer preference for branded hospitality experiences
- Tier-II and Tier-III cities are emerging as hospitality markets on improving connectivity, rising disposable incomes and branded-chain expansion
- Watch-items on the outlook: the Israel-Iran conflict feeding oil prices and inflation (India imports most of its crude, and the RBI may turn cautious on rate cuts), rising costs of food, utilities and wages, and competition from short-term rentals such as Airbnb
- Management's own conclusion: for 2026-27 the hotel industry outlook is broadly positive in India, but profitability will depend on how effectively hotels manage rising costs, technology adoption, sustainability expectations and evolving traveller preferences

risks.risk: The Saraf Group's option to acquire Hyatt Regency, Mumbai, and the unresolved classification of the funding it advanced
risks.note: Novak Hotels Private Limited ('Saraf Group') advanced amounts to the Company under a framework agreement entered into between the promoters and the Saraf Group during the insolvency resolution process, and the agreement gives the Saraf Group an option to acquire Hyatt Regency, Mumbai. The Board obtained shareholder approval to create a charge/lien over the hotel to secure those amounts, and Novak's own audited accounts describe them as advances for acquiring the hotel - so the auditors are 'unable to state if the classification of amounts received is' appropriate. risks.risk: Cost, labour and demand risks management flags for the hotel business

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Asian Hotels (West) Limited is a single-segment hotel owner whose own property, Hotel Hyatt Regency in Mumbai, is still shut after the company emerged from CIRP, while its material subsidiary Aria Hotels owns the 523-room JW Marriott at New Delhi Aerocity.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: The Company is engaged in only one segment, the Hotel Business. It owns Hotel Hyatt Regency in Mumbai, which is in shut condition as on date, and the Company's own operations had not yet started after coming out from CIRP during the year under review; the Company was revived on 9th January 2024 and management has since been engaged in completing pending compliances with BSE, NSE and other authorities. Its economic activity is carried on through its 99.98% subsidiary Aria Hotels and Consultancy Services Private Limited, which owns a 523-room 5-star deluxe hotel operated under the J.W. Marriott brand at New Delhi Aerocity, Hospitality District, near IGI Airport, and whose principal activity is the development, design, finance, construction, operation and maintenance of upscale and luxury hotel property in India.

group_structure.title: Group structure (subsidiaries / JV / related parties)
group_structure.body:
- Aria Hotels and Consultancy Services Private Limited (ARIA) — subsidiary: The Company's only subsidiary and a material subsidiary; 99.98% proportion of ownership interest and voting power held by the Company as at March 31, 2026 (99.98% as at March 31, 2025); place of incorporation and place of operation India; unquoted. Principal activity per the notes: development, design, finance, construction, operation and maintenance of upscale and luxury hotel property. Per the Directors' Report, ARIA is the owner of a 523-room 5-star deluxe hotel under the J.W. Marriott brand at New Delhi Aerocity, Hospitality District, near IGI Airport. Reporting period 31st March 2026, same as the holding company. Related-party dealings during the year comprised services availed (reimbursement of GST), rent paid, reimbursement of expenses, and year-end balances including a security deposit - amounts not reproduced. Part B of Form AOC-1 (associates and joint ventures) is marked Not Applicable and the Company had no associate or joint venture company during the year or as on 31st March 2026.
- Novak Hotels Private Limited (referred to as the 'Saraf Group' or 'lender') — related party: Named in the Directors'/auditor material in the wider annual report (not in the standalone RPT note) as the party that advanced funds to the Company under a framework agreement entered into between the promoters of the Company and the Saraf Group as part of the insolvency resolution process; the framework agreement provides the Saraf Group an option to acquire Hyatt Regency, Mumbai, and shareholder approval was obtained to create a charge/lien over that hotel. The Company states it is not a party to the framework agreement. Amounts not reproduced here.
- Mr. Sandeep Gupta — related party: Key Management Personnel - Chairman & Non-Executive Director (DIN 00057942); signs the Directors' Report and Form AOC-1. Carries a director remuneration payable year-end balance.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body: - **Hotel Business:** Hotel Hyatt Regency, Mumbai (owned by the Company; shut as on date), JW Marriott New Delhi Aerocity (523-room 5-star deluxe hotel, owned by subsidiary Aria Hotels), ADRIFT Kaya (Japanese specialty restaurant), Delhi Baking Company (bakery/patisserie), Spa by JW

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- India - luxury / 5-star deluxe hotel accommodation
- New Delhi Aerocity (Hospitality District, near IGI Airport)
- Mumbai
- Weddings and social events (JW Marriott New Delhi Aerocity recognised as a wedding venue)
- Luxury food and beverage / spa services within the hotel

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- India's hotel industry is projected to grow between 9% and 12% during FY2026, driven by strong occupancy levels and improved average room rates, with demand expected to remain resilient despite a high base effect
- Premium hotel occupancy is expected to remain robust in the range of 72-74%, while room tariffs are anticipated to witness steady growth owing to demand outpacing new supply additions in major cities
- Demand growth continued to outpace room supply in several key markets, leading to improved pricing power for hotel operators; premium room inventory growth may continue to lag demand growth over the next few years, supporting occupancy and pricing
- Demand base is domestic leisure tourism, destination weddings, religious tourism, concerts, sporting events, corporate travel and MICE; India's hospitality sector is becoming increasingly domestic-demand driven
- Sector tailwinds from increasing air connectivity, infrastructure development, digital travel platforms and rising consumer preference for branded hospitality experiences
- Tier-II and Tier-III cities are emerging as hospitality markets on improving connectivity, rising disposable incomes and branded-chain expansion
- Watch-items on the outlook: the Israel-Iran conflict feeding oil prices and inflation (India imports most of its crude, and the RBI may turn cautious on rate cuts), rising costs of food, utilities and wages, and competition from short-term rentals such as Airbnb
- Management's own conclusion: for 2026-27 the hotel industry outlook is broadly positive in India, but profitability will depend on how effectively hotels manage rising costs, technology adoption, sustainability expectations and evolving traveller preferences

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Restart the shut Hyatt Regency, Mumbai hotel: the Company is in the process of evaluating property, plant and equipment by physical verification, including the location of each item, before commencing operation
- Complete the backlog of pending compliances with BSE, NSE and other concerned authorities following the Company's revival on 9th January 2024
- Restore market access for the stock: after approval of the resolution plan the Company applied to BSE Limited and the National Stock Exchange of India Limited for revocation of suspension of trading of its shares and obtained approval from both exchanges
- Continue to hold and consolidate the JW Marriott New Delhi Aerocity asset through the 99.98% material subsidiary Aria Hotels and Consultancy Services Private Limited, which is the Company's only subsidiary and its only operating hotel

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Ownership of two land-anchored luxury hotel assets in the two largest Indian hospitality markets - Hotel Hyatt Regency in Mumbai (direct) and the JW Marriott at New Delhi Aerocity (through Aria Hotels)
- The Aerocity asset operates under an international luxury brand (J.W. Marriott) in a supply-constrained airport hospitality district
- Demonstrated brand strength of the Aerocity asset: JW Marriott New Delhi Aerocity won 'Best Luxury Hotel' at India's Best Awards 2025 by Travel & Leisure, its Mosaic Impact Award under the Luxury Segment from Marriott International, and its outlets (ADRIFT Kaya, Delhi Baking Company, Spa by JW) carried separate industry awards in 2025
